Subject: Inference constraints & topology — follow-up and technical asks

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call this morning. Below is a concise synthesis of the constraints you described and the technical asks we agreed to action. I copied Marissa and Karthik so we have SE and CS context.

Quick summary of customer goals (ForwardPay):
- Reduce per-transaction inference cost while keeping 95th percentile latency under 200ms for single-chat completions.
- Support a peak authentication traffic spike of ~350 QPS for a 2-minute burst without degraded tail latency.
- Keep PII out of indexed logs; prefer KV cache + ephemeral tokens for session state.

Primary pain points you called out:
- Current vendor shows P95 = 320ms at 120 QPS.
- No ability to route sensitive flows into private VPC; logs are retained longer than policy.
- Model hallucination on long receipts (>1,000 tokens) that causes manual review.

Items we committed to follow up on (action owners in parentheses):
1) Send an SLO matrix with concrete targets and trade-offs for 3 topology options: hosted with private tenant + finer-grained routing, dedicated GPU pool, and on-prem appliance (Sean).
2) Provide an estimated throughput cost model for Llama-3-Chat-13B quantized paths (Karthik). Include batch sizing, expected token/sec, and recommended quantization (4-bit vs 8-bit) with quality caveats.
3) Draft a minimal network diagram showing a VPC private-control-plane pattern and how telemetry is forwarded to ForwardPay's Splunk instance (Marissa).
4) Share a short checklist of required security artifacts (SOC-2 evidence, retention controls, KMS integration points) for procurement (Sean).

Critical technical notes from the call:
- Target latency SLO: P95 <= 180ms for auth path (sequence length ~256), tail P99 <= 400ms.
- Sustained throughput requirement: 120 QPS; burst capacity: 300–350 QPS for up to 2 minutes.
- Typical input sequence length: average 120 tokens, peak 1,200 tokens in invoice parsing flows.
- Preferred model family: Llama-3-Chat-13B (customer will also pilot a distilled 7B variant for low-cost flows).
- KV / prefix caching is acceptable for non-PII flows; PII flows must use ephemeral cache and not persist to disk.

Attachments: forwarding two reference artifacts in the next message: SLO matrix (spreadsheet) and a rough topology sketch.

Next step: I’ll attach the matrix and a topology sketch by EOD PT. Can you confirm which flows must be private VPC-only and which can be hosted? That will let us size dedicated capacity vs hosted burst.

Cheers,
Sean

Thanks, Sean — this captures the call well. Quick clarifications:
- The auth path is private VPC-only because it touches cardholder data in the tokenized payload. Any inference for auth must run inside our VPC or on-prem.
- Receipt/invoice parsing can be hosted, but we need redaction hooks and a guaranteed 24-hour window for logs retention before deletion.
- For burst behavior: the 350 QPS number is a worst-case estimate; typical day-to-day peak is 160 QPS.

I attached the SLO inputs we keep internally (small spreadsheet) and a screenshot of our existing edge topology. They are attachments in this thread: forwardpay_slo_matrix.xlsx and existing_edge.png.

Two asks for you:
1) If you can provide a cost delta estimate for running the auth flow entirely in a private VPC vs hosted with an encrypted tunnel. Even a ballpark monthly delta is helpful.
2) Any notes on model distillation/quality tradeoffs for the 7B we’ll pilot. Do you have examples of retrieval-augmented patterns that preserve accuracy for invoice fields?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’d like the procurement checklist by early next week.

Hi Laura — quick technical response to your two asks, and a short runbook we suggest for the pilot.

1) Cost delta (ballpark) — private VPC vs hosted tunnel:
- Private VPC dedicated pool (reserved capacity): estimated incremental cost ~ $24k–$32k/month for the auth path at 120 sustained QPS with 2:1 reserve for burst. This assumes reserved 4x A100-equivalent capacity with autoscaling buffer.
- Hosted with encrypted tunnel + burst: estimated incremental cost ~ $6k–$9k/month but with no SLA for VPC isolation; logs would still transit our control plane unless you opt for Private deployment.

2) Distillation / 7B tradeoffs:
- 7B distilled model yields ~2–4% drop in entity extraction F1 on our invoice dataset vs 13B full model in our tests. For fields with structured patterns (dates, amounts) gap is minimal; free-text normalization suffered more.
- Recommended approach: use the 7B distilled model for low-risk hosted flows and route high-risk auth and long-document parsing to the 13B quantized path in private/dedicated environments.

3) Retrieval-augmented pattern: local RAG with two-level store:
- Short-term KV cache for session context (ephemeral).
- Document store (search) for invoice templates + historical extractions; normalize fields via deterministic parsers post-generation.

4) Pilot runbook (high level):
- Week 0: Deploy private VPC pilot for auth path (minimal topology, 2 replicas, instrument P95/P99).
- Week 1: Run synthetic traffic (120 QPS sustained, 350 QPS 2-min spikes) and gather latency, error, and cost telemetry.
- Week 2: Run A/B with 7B hosted vs 13B private on a 10% traffic split for invoice flows. Monitor entity-level F1 and human-review rate.

I’ll attach a rough topology PNG and a short SLO matrix (Sean will forward the spreadsheet formally).
